questions.question: Your raw Messages API loop ends as soon as a response contains a text block. Users report the agent stops right after writing "Let me check the inventory system." What should the loop do instead?

options.text: Stop only when the text includes a completion phrase such as "task complete" or "I'm done".
options.why_wrong: Natural-language completion signals are unreliable; Claude may phrase things differently or keep calling tools after such text.

options.text: Keep looping while stop_reason is "tool_use", run every tool_use block, and stop on "end_turn".
Raise the iteration cap to 50 so the agent gets more turns before the loop exits on its own.
options.why_wrong: The text check ends the loop, not the cap. An iteration cap is only a safety bound, never the primary stop signal.

options.text: Strip text blocks from any response that also holds tool_use blocks, then check for completion.
options.why_wrong: This hides the model's reasoning and still keys termination on content instead of stop_reason.

questions.explanation: Claude often writes text and requests tools in the same turn. The termination signal is stop_reason: execute all tool_use blocks and append matching tool_result blocks while it is "tool_use", and stop on "end_turn". Other values (max_tokens, pause_turn, refusal) need explicit handling.
questions.key_takeaway: Drive the loop with stop_reason: continue on tool_use, stop on end_turn, and never parse text for completion.

questions.question: A request using a server-side tool (web search) comes back with stop_reason "pause_turn" after many search iterations. What should your loop do next?

options.text: Treat it like end_turn and return the partial text to the user as the final answer.
options.why_wrong: pause_turn means the server-tool loop hit its iteration limit, not that Claude finished the task.

options.text: Run the server tool yourself and append a tool_result block for each pending call.
options.why_wrong: Server tools execute on Anthropic's side; you continue by sending the content back, not by executing them.

options.text: Retry the original request from scratch with a larger max_tokens value to avoid it.
options.why_wrong: pause_turn is not a token-cap signal (that is max_tokens), and restarting throws away the progress made.

options.text: Send the assistant content back unchanged in a new request so Claude can continue.

questions.explanation: pause_turn is returned when a server-tool loop reaches its iteration limit mid-turn. The response is incomplete but valid: append it as the assistant turn and call the API again so Claude can resume where it paused.
questions.key_takeaway: On pause_turn, send the assistant content back unchanged so Claude can continue the paused server-tool turn.

questions.question: A Python service calls query() with max_turns=8. Some runs end with a ResultMessage whose subtype is "error_max_turns", and the code that reads message.result crashes. What is the right handling?

options.text: Read result anyway, because on error subtypes it holds a summary of the partial work done.
options.why_wrong: The result field is present only when subtype is "success".

options.text: Remove max_turns entirely so the SDK can never produce an error result on long tasks.
options.why_wrong: Safety bounds should stay, and other error subtypes (budget, execution, structured output) still occur.

options.text: Check subtype first; result exists only on success. Keep session_id to resume with a higher cap.
Catch the error and start a new session, since a session that hit an error cannot be resumed.
options.why_wrong: Every ResultMessage carries session_id, so you can resume the same session after an error.

questions.explanation: ResultMessage.subtype is success, error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution or error_max_structured_output_retries, and result is only set on success. Every result still carries session_id, total_cost_usd, usage and num_turns, and single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result, so wrap it and resume if needed.
questions.key_takeaway: Branch on ResultMessage.subtype before reading result; error results still give you session_id to resume.

questions.question: A multi-tenant service built on the Agent SDK omits settingSources. On a shared build host, agents start following one developer's personal hooks and CLAUDE.md preferences. What explains this and what is the fix?

options.text: Omitting settingSources loads user, project and local settings like the CLI; pass [] for isolation.
The SDK always loads user settings and ignores settingSources, so delete ~/.claude on every build host.
options.why_wrong: settingSources does control filesystem loading; [] disables user, project and local sources.

options.text: Omitting settingSources loads nothing, so the hooks must come from managed settings on the build host.
options.why_wrong: Current docs: omitting it loads the same filesystem settings as the CLI, not nothing.

options.text: Hooks leak only through subagents, so set omitClaudeMd on every AgentDefinition to stop the leakage.
options.why_wrong: omitClaudeMd affects CLAUDE.md for a subagent; it doesn't stop user-level hooks and settings loading.

questions.explanation: When settingSources is omitted, query() loads user, project and local settings, CLAUDE.md and .claude/ skills, agents and commands, matching the CLI. Pass settingSources: [] (setting_sources=[] in Python) to disable user/project/local files, and for full multi-tenant isolation also set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY="1", a per-tenant CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and strict_mcp_config=True.
questions.key_takeaway: Pass setting_sources=[] plus CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY="1", per-tenant CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and strict_mcp_config=True.

questions.question: An SDK app passes allowedTools: ["Bash"] and a canUseTool callback that should reject any command touching /prod. The callback never fires and a /prod command runs. What is the right fix?

options.text: Move the check into a PreToolUse hook, which runs first on every call; avoid bare allowedTools entries.
Set permissionMode to bypassPermissions so that every tool call is routed through canUseTool for review.
options.why_wrong: bypassPermissions auto-approves calls before the callback is consulted, making the problem worse.

options.text: Set permissionMode to dontAsk so the SDK invokes canUseTool silently instead of showing a user prompt.
options.why_wrong: In dontAsk mode the canUseTool step is skipped and unapproved calls are denied outright.

options.text: Add disallowedTools: ["Bash"] alongside allowedTools so the callback is consulted for conflicting entries.
options.why_wrong: A bare entry in disallowedTools removes Bash from context entirely; it does not route calls through the callback.

questions.explanation: canUseTool fires only when the harness would otherwise prompt. A bare allowedTools: ["Bash"] entry pre-approves every Bash call, so canUseTool is never reached (TypeScript emits CLAUDE_SDK_CAN_USE_TOOL_SHADOWED). A PreToolUse hook runs on every matching call, and a scoped disallowedTools rule such as "Bash(*prod*)" denies matching calls in every mode.
questions.key_takeaway: canUseTool fires only when a prompt would appear; use a PreToolUse hook or scoped disallowedTools rule to gate every call.

questions.question: You build a Python Agent SDK service with an in-process tool lookup_order registered via @tool and create_sdk_mcp_server(name="orders", tools=[lookup_order]). You want Claude to ONLY see and call lookup_order (no built-in tools like Bash, Read, or Edit in its context window) and execute it without prompting in default mode. Which ClaudeAgentOptions setup works?

options.text: ClaudeAgentOptions(mcp_servers={"orders": server}, allowed_tools=["lookup_order"], permission_mode="default")
options.why_wrong: Omitting tools leaves all built-in tool schemas in Claude's context window, and SDK MCP tools must be referenced as mcp__orders__lookup_order.

options.text: ClaudeAgentOptions(allowed_tools=["mcp__orders__lookup_order"], disallowed_tools=["Bash(*)", "Edit(*)"])
options.why_wrong: Scoped rules in disallowed_tools keep the tools in context, and other built-in tools (Read, Glob, Grep, WebFetch) remain available.

options.text: ClaudeAgentOptions(tools=[], mcp_servers={"orders": server}, allowed_tools=["mcp__orders__lookup_order"])
ClaudeAgentOptions(tools=["mcp__orders__lookup_order"], mcp_servers={"orders": server}, permission_mode="dontAsk")
options.why_wrong: tools only configures built-in tool availability; MCP tools must be pre-approved in allowed_tools as mcp__<server>__<tool>.

questions.explanation: In ClaudeAgentOptions, tools controls which built-in tools are in the context window: tools=[] strips them all so Claude sees only MCP tools, whereas allowed_tools only pre-approves calls and leaves unlisted built-ins visible. In-process tools created with create_sdk_mcp_server(name="orders", ...) are exposed as mcp__orders__lookup_order and pre-approved via allowed_tools.
questions.key_takeaway: Use tools=[] to strip built-in tools from context, and pre-approve in-process SDK MCP tools in allowed_tools as mcp__<server>__<tool>.

questions.question: Bills for a monorepo agent occasionally spike. Logs show subagents spawning their own subagents four layers deep. Which configuration bounds this most directly?

options.text: Set max_turns=5 on the main query so it stops before any deep delegation can start.
options.why_wrong: max_turns counts the main loop's turns; each child runs its own loop, so depth and spend stay open.

options.text: Delete the word "delegate" from every AgentDefinition description to discourage spawning.
options.why_wrong: Descriptions guide routing; they do not remove the Agent tool or cap the tree.

options.text: Set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH low (e.g. 1) and cap spend with max_budget_usd.
Raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS so the trees finish sooner and cost less.
options.why_wrong: That limit caps how many run at once; more concurrency does not reduce total spend.

questions.explanation: Subagents can spawn subagents. The SDK bounds the tree with a spawn-depth limit (default 3; 1 stops children from spawning), a concurrency limit (default 20) and an optional max_budget_usd that counts subagent spend.
questions.key_takeaway: Bound agent trees with spawn depth and a budget cap, not with prompt wording.

questions.question: You define two subagents, "db-reviewer" and "sql-reviewer", both described as "Reviews database code." Claude hands migration reviews to either one seemingly at random. What is the best fix?

options.text: Rewrite each description as a distinct "use when…" line: migrations vs ORM code.
Give both agents model="opus" so that Claude can judge better which one should review.
options.why_wrong: The model setting picks what runs the subagent; it does not change how Claude routes to it.

options.text: Copy both agents' prompts into the main system prompt and stop using subagents for it.
options.why_wrong: That gives up context isolation instead of fixing the ambiguous routing.

options.text: Set background=True on one agent so that Claude learns to prefer the other one instead.
options.why_wrong: background controls blocking behaviour, not which agent Claude selects.

questions.explanation: Claude chooses a subagent from its description, which is the required field that says when to use it. Two identical descriptions give it nothing to choose by; make each one name the situations it owns.
questions.key_takeaway: AgentDefinition.description drives delegation; make descriptions mutually exclusive.

questions.question: A nightly job must lint, type-check and then summarize results for the same repository, always in that order. A teammate proposes one agent that decides at runtime which subagents to spawn. What fits better?

options.text: Agent-led delegation, since letting the model choose always gives better coverage.
options.why_wrong: When the order never changes, runtime choice adds cost and variance without adding value.

options.text: Launch one subagent per step in parallel so all three steps finish at the same time.
options.why_wrong: The summary depends on the first two steps, so they are not independent.

options.text: A single query with tool_choice forced to the lint tool on every turn of the run.
options.why_wrong: Forcing a tool every turn stops the agent from finishing, and it only ever lints.

options.text: Run the three steps as a fixed sequence of query() calls in your own code.

questions.explanation: When the steps and their order are known in advance, encode them as a workflow in code. Agent-led delegation earns its cost when the next step depends on what was just found.
questions.key_takeaway: Use a coded workflow for fixed sequences and agent-led delegation for open-ended work.

questions.question: A coordinator spawns a "log-scanner" subagent and immediately reads the Agent tool result, expecting findings. The result shows status "async_launched" and no report. What is going on?

options.text: The subagent crashed at startup, and async_launched is the generic failure status.
options.why_wrong: async_launched acknowledges a successful background launch; it is not an error status.

options.text: Agent is missing from allowed_tools, so the call is queued until someone approves it.
options.why_wrong: An unapproved call is denied or routed to the permission flow; it is not reported as launched.

options.text: Subagents run in the background by default; the report arrives in a later turn.
The coordinator's max_turns is too low, so the report was cut down to a status line.
options.why_wrong: Hitting max_turns ends the parent loop with error_max_turns; it does not shorten a subagent report.

questions.explanation: By default a spawned subagent runs as a background task: the Agent tool result says async_launched and the subagent's final message arrives later. Treat the launch result as an acknowledgement, not as the answer.
questions.key_takeaway: async_launched means the subagent is running in the background; wait for its report.

questions.question: A parent agent has already captured a failing test name and its stack trace. It delegates "fix the failing test" to a fresh "fixer" subagent, which then spends many turns re-running the whole suite. What is the most direct fix?

options.text: Copy the test name, stack trace and suspect paths into the Agent tool's prompt.
Set the fixer's model to "inherit" so that it shares the parent's conversation.
options.why_wrong: model only picks which model runs the subagent; it does not share any conversation history.

options.text: Add the stack trace to the parent's system prompt so every subagent inherits it.
options.why_wrong: A non-fork subagent does not receive the parent's system prompt or its history.

options.text: Raise the fixer's maxTurns so that it has room to find the failure by itself.
options.why_wrong: That pays for rediscovery instead of passing what the parent already knows.

questions.explanation: A non-fork subagent starts fresh: it sees its own system prompt, project CLAUDE.md and the Agent tool's prompt string. Anything the parent learned must be copied into that prompt; references like "the error above" point at nothing.
questions.key_takeaway: The Agent prompt string is the only way to hand a fresh subagent what the parent already knows.

questions.question: A custom "endpoint-mapper" subagent spent 30 turns cataloguing an API. An hour later, in a new query() call, you ask a follow-up and the mapper starts from scratch. How do you continue from its earlier work?

options.text: Set background=True on the AgentDefinition so the mapper stays alive between calls.
options.why_wrong: background makes a subagent non-blocking inside a session; it does not carry state into a new session.

options.text: Define an AgentDefinition with the same name; the SDK reuses that agent's transcript.
options.why_wrong: Agent names do not link transcripts, and each query() call starts a new session by default.

options.text: Pass fork_session=True so the SDK attaches the most recent subagent to the new call.
options.why_wrong: fork_session needs a session ID and copies the parent conversation; it does not target a subagent.

options.text: Resume the original session_id and name the earlier result's agentId in the new prompt.

questions.explanation: A custom subagent's Agent tool result ends with an agentId trailer. Resume the same session with resume=session_id and reference that agent ID in the prompt; the subagent continues with its full history of tool calls and reasoning.
questions.key_takeaway: Capture session_id and agentId to resume a subagent instead of re-running its exploration.

questions.question: A PreToolUse hook rewrites every Write file_path to live under /sandbox. It returns updatedInput together with permissionDecision "defer" so a reviewer can look later. After resuming, files land at their original paths. Why?

options.text: updatedInput must sit at the top level of the hook output, outside hookSpecificOutput.
options.why_wrong: It is the reverse: updatedInput belongs inside hookSpecificOutput.

options.text: "defer" drops updatedInput; pair the rewrite with "allow" or "ask", or omit the decision.
Hooks can rewrite input only for MCP tools; built-in tools such as Write ignore it.
options.why_wrong: updatedInput works for built-in tools; rewriting a Write path is a standard use.

options.text: The matcher should be lowercase "write", so the hook never ran for these calls.
options.why_wrong: Tool names are case-sensitive and the built-in tool is "Write"; the hook did run.

questions.explanation: updatedInput is applied with "allow" (auto-approve), with "ask" (show for approval) or with no decision (normal permission evaluation). Returning "defer" ends the turn with stop_reason tool_deferred and discards the modified input.
questions.key_takeaway: Never pair updatedInput with "defer"; the rewrite is dropped.

doc_links.label: Hooks in the Claude Agent SDK

questions.question: Three backend tools return dates as Unix epoch, ISO 8601 and "MM/DD/YY". The agent sometimes compares dates wrongly. Where should you normalize them?

options.text: In a PostToolUse hook that rewrites each tool's output to one format before Claude reads it.
In the system prompt, with a table that explains how to convert each date format by hand.
options.why_wrong: This leaves conversion to the model, which is probabilistic and error-prone.

options.text: In a PreToolUse hook that rewrites the input arguments of every tool call to ISO 8601.
options.why_wrong: Rewriting inputs does not change the formats the tools return.

options.text: In a final review subagent that re-checks every date comparison after the answer is done.
options.why_wrong: This adds cost and catches errors late instead of fixing the data at its source.

questions.explanation: PostToolUse hooks can replace output (updatedToolOutput) or append context before the model sees a result. Normalizing heterogeneous formats there gives the model consistent data on every call.
questions.key_takeaway: Use PostToolUse hooks to normalize tool output deterministically before the model sees it.

doc_links.label: Hooks in the Claude Agent SDK

questions.question: A ClaudeSDKClient app calls interrupt() when a user clicks Stop, then immediately sends a new query and calls receive_response() once. The UI shows the old task's messages instead of the new answer. Why?

options.text: interrupt() closes the session, so the new query starts fresh and replays old history.
options.why_wrong: The session stays open after an interrupt; nothing is replayed.

options.text: interrupt() leaves buffered messages; drain them through the old ResultMessage first.
Every query after an interrupt must pass resume=session_id to reach the new turn.
options.why_wrong: ClaudeSDKClient keeps the same session, so resume is not needed.

options.text: interrupt() only works with single-shot query(), so this call was silently ignored.
options.why_wrong: It is the reverse: interrupt() works only in streaming mode, which ClaudeSDKClient uses.

questions.explanation: interrupt() sends a stop signal but does not clear the message buffer. Messages the interrupted task already produced, including its ResultMessage, stay in the stream and must be drained with receive_response() before reading the reply to the next query.
questions.key_takeaway: After interrupt(), drain the interrupted turn up to its ResultMessage before reading new output.

questions.question: A multi-turn SDK worker is restarted by a deploy between two user requests. You stored session_id from the last ResultMessage. What restores the conversation for the next request?

options.text: Call query() with resume=session_id (or continue_conversation=True).
Call query() with fork_session=True and no ID so the SDK picks the newest transcript.
options.why_wrong: fork_session needs a session ID and creates a new branch rather than continuing.

options.text: Paste the previous transcript text into the new prompt string so nothing is lost.
options.why_wrong: That inflates the prompt and loses the structured history that resume restores.

options.text: Nothing special: query() reattaches to the most recent session in the directory.
options.why_wrong: query() starts a new session by default unless you pass continue or resume.

questions.explanation: Sessions persist on disk. resume=session_id reopens a specific session with its full history; continue_conversation=True picks the most recent one in the working directory. File changes made earlier are not rolled back.
questions.key_takeaway: Persist session_id and resume it after a restart; query() starts fresh by default.

questions.question: An in-process stock_level tool returns "0 units" whenever the inventory API times out. During an incident the agent places restock orders for items that are actually in stock. What should the handler do on a timeout?

options.text: Let the exception propagate so the SDK ends the query before any order goes out.
options.why_wrong: An uncaught handler exception becomes an error result and the loop keeps going; nothing is terminated.

options.text: Return "0 units (approximate)" so the model knows to treat the number with care.
options.why_wrong: It is still a number, and Claude can still act on it as a fact.

options.text: Catch it and return is_error: True, saying the count is unknown and when to retry.
Retry inside the handler in a loop with no limit until the inventory API responds.
options.why_wrong: That stalls the turn indefinitely and still tells Claude nothing about the outage.

questions.explanation: A value of zero is a valid answer, so Claude treats it as fact. Mark the call as failed with is_error and say the value is unknown, plus a retry hint. Handler errors never stop the loop, so the message you compose is what Claude reasons about.
questions.key_takeaway: Unknown is not zero: report backend failures with is_error and say what is unknown.

questions.question: A create_ticket tool rejects calls because the project key has the wrong case ("ops" instead of "OPS"). It returns is_error with "Request failed", and Claude gives up and apologizes. Which error text best helps Claude recover?

options.text: "Invalid project key 'ops'. Keys are uppercase; valid keys: OPS, SEC, WEB."
"Request failed, please try again later." so the agent knows to retry the call.
options.why_wrong: It implies a transient fault; retrying with the same arguments fails again.

options.text: Return success with an empty ticket ID so that the agent's loop is not interrupted.
options.why_wrong: Claude would report a ticket that does not exist.

options.text: "Error 400" with the raw HTTP status code and nothing else in the message body.
options.why_wrong: A bare status code does not say what to change.

questions.explanation: Write the error for the next decision: when Claude can fix the problem by changing arguments, say exactly what was wrong and what values are accepted. Vague or retry-flavoured messages lead to giving up or useless retries.
questions.key_takeaway: If Claude can fix the call, the error message should say exactly how.

questions.question: A subagent that summarizes CI failures was given Bash so it could curl the CI API. Logs show it sometimes runs unrelated commands, such as deleting cache directories. Which change best applies least privilege?

options.text: Keep Bash and add "only use curl against the CI API" to the subagent's prompt.
options.why_wrong: A prompt instruction is guidance, not a guarantee; Bash stays fully available.

options.text: Switch the session to acceptEdits so that destructive commands get reviewed first.
options.why_wrong: acceptEdits auto-approves file operations; it widens access rather than narrowing it.

options.text: Give the subagent every built-in tool so it never needs a Bash workaround again.
options.why_wrong: More tools mean more schema tokens and more room for misuse.

options.text: Swap Bash for an in-process get_build_log(job_id) tool; set tools to Read plus that tool.

questions.explanation: Scope each subagent to the narrowest tools its role needs. An in-process tool enforces the boundary in code (one job's log, read-only), and AgentDefinition.tools keeps Bash out of the subagent's context entirely.
questions.key_takeaway: Replace broad tools with narrow in-process tools when misuse is the risk.

questions.question: Claude issues four calls to your in-process get_price tool in one turn, but they execute one after another and add seconds of latency. The tool only reads data. What lets them run concurrently?

options.text: Set permission_mode="acceptEdits" so that the four calls are approved as one batch.
options.why_wrong: Permission modes decide approval, not whether calls execute concurrently.

options.text: Wrap the handler body in asyncio.gather so the tool runs its own calls in parallel.
options.why_wrong: Each call is a separate handler invocation; gather inside one call cannot overlap the others.

options.text: Add annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True) to the @tool definition.
Register get_price as four separate tools so each call can get its own worker.
options.why_wrong: Custom tools run sequentially by default no matter how many there are.

questions.explanation: Read-only built-ins such as Read, Glob and Grep can run concurrently, while custom tools default to sequential execution. Marking a custom tool readOnlyHint lets Claude batch it with other read-only calls. Keep the hint accurate; it is not enforced.
questions.key_takeaway: Set readOnlyHint on read-only custom tools so their calls can run in parallel.

questions.question: A worker uses allowed_tools=["Read", "Grep"] with permission_mode="bypassPermissions" to stay "read-only". An audit shows it ran Bash and Edit. Why?

options.text: bypassPermissions ignores allowed_tools only when a canUseTool callback is also set.
options.why_wrong: There is no such condition; the callback is not the reason unlisted tools ran.

options.text: allowed_tools only pre-approves; unlisted tools fall to the mode, which approves them.
Read and Grep call Bash internally, and Bash inherits their pre-approval at runtime.
options.why_wrong: Built-in tools do not pass approval to other tools.

options.text: allowed_tools applies only to subagents; the main agent reads settings.json instead.
options.why_wrong: allowed_tools applies to the main session as well.

questions.explanation: allowed_tools adds allow rules; it does not restrict anything. Calls that match no rule reach the permission-mode step, and bypassPermissions approves them. For a read-only worker, limit tools in context (tools=[...]) or pair allowed_tools with dontAsk.
questions.key_takeaway: allowed_tools does not constrain bypassPermissions; restrict with tools, deny rules or dontAsk.

questions.question: A research agent is configured with tools=["Read", "Glob", "Grep"] and a canUseTool callback written to handle clarifying questions. Claude never asks anything and guesses between ambiguous options. What is missing?

options.text: permission_mode must be "plan", since clarifying questions exist only in planning.
options.why_wrong: AskUserQuestion is available outside plan mode.

options.text: The callback must return PermissionResultDeny so Claude rephrases its call as a question.
options.why_wrong: A deny blocks a call; it does not make Claude ask the user anything.

options.text: "AskUserQuestion" has to be in the explicit tools list; leaving it out hides the tool.
A UserPromptSubmit hook must forward each question to the canUseTool callback.
options.why_wrong: That hook fires when a prompt is submitted, not when Claude asks something.

questions.explanation: Clarifying questions go through the AskUserQuestion tool, which reaches canUseTool like any approval. It is available by default, but an explicit tools list hides everything not listed, so include "AskUserQuestion" and return answers keyed by question text.
questions.key_takeaway: With an explicit tools list, include AskUserQuestion or Claude cannot ask.

questions.question: A "migration-auditor" subagent with maxTurns=15 returns output marked partial after covering two of three services. What should the coordinator do to finish the audit most efficiently?

options.text: Resume that subagent by its agentId so it keeps its history and covers the last service.
Spawn a new auditor with the same prompt and maxTurns=30 to redo the whole audit.
options.why_wrong: It throws away two services of finished work and pays for them again.

options.text: Treat the report as complete, since the SDK marks output partial only for optional work.
options.why_wrong: Partial means the turn limit was reached before the work finished.

options.text: Raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS so that the auditor is given more turns.
options.why_wrong: That setting caps simultaneous subagents; it does not change any agent's turns.

questions.explanation: When a subagent reaches maxTurns, its output comes back marked partial and it can be resumed. Resuming by agentId keeps its tool results and reasoning, so it only has to cover what is left.
questions.key_takeaway: Resume a partial subagent by agentId instead of starting over.

questions.question: Deep into a long debugging session, the agent starts proposing "typical" fixes that ignore the specific classes it identified an hour earlier. What helps most from here on?

options.text: Paste the whole earlier transcript back in as a new message so that nothing gets forgotten.
options.why_wrong: This adds more volume to an already degraded context.

options.text: Keep findings in a scratchpad file it re-reads; delegate verbose exploration to subagents.
Raise max_tokens so that the model has more room to recall the findings from earlier on.
options.why_wrong: max_tokens caps output length; it does not improve recall of earlier context.

options.text: Ask the agent to rate its confidence in each fix before it applies any of the changes.
options.why_wrong: Self-rated confidence does not restore the specific facts that have been lost.

questions.explanation: Context degradation shows up as generic answers and forgotten specifics. Persist findings in a scratchpad file, delegate noisy exploration to subagents so only summaries return, and use /compact or phase summaries for long sessions.
questions.key_takeaway: Persist key findings outside the context and delegate verbose exploration to subagents.

questions.question: A long-running agent was told in its first prompt never to touch files under vendor/. Hours later, after a compact_boundary message appears in the stream, it edits vendor/ files. What is the most robust fix?

options.text: Repeat the rule in every user message so that a recent copy is always present.
options.why_wrong: It helps sometimes, but it is still a prompt rule and costs tokens on every turn.

options.text: Raise max_turns so the history never gets long enough to be summarized at all.
options.why_wrong: max_turns bounds the loop; it does not control when compaction happens.

options.text: Send /compact by hand at the start so automatic compaction never runs later on.
options.why_wrong: Manual compaction does not prevent later automatic compaction, and it summarizes the rule too.

options.text: Move the rule to CLAUDE.md and add a PreToolUse deny for any write under vendor/.

questions.explanation: Compaction replaces older history with a summary, so instructions from early in the conversation can be lost. Persistent rules belong in CLAUDE.md (loaded via setting_sources), and rules that must always hold belong in a hook.
questions.key_takeaway: Keep durable rules in CLAUDE.md and enforce must-hold rules with hooks, not the first prompt.

questions.question: Your app needs the agent's final answer as JSON that matches a schema and is validated before your code reads it. Which approach fits the Agent SDK?

options.text: Ask for JSON in the prompt and pull it out of ResultMessage.result with a regex.
options.why_wrong: Nothing validates the output, so malformed or partial JSON reaches your code.

options.text: Pass output_format with a json_schema and read ResultMessage.structured_output.
Force tool_choice to a dummy tool on every turn so Claude always has to emit JSON.
options.why_wrong: Forcing a tool every turn stops the agent from finishing, and it is a Messages API setting.

options.text: Register a PostToolUse hook that converts the agent's final text answer into JSON.
options.why_wrong: PostToolUse runs after tool calls, not on the final answer.

questions.explanation: output_format={"type": "json_schema", "schema": ...} makes the SDK validate the final result and expose it as ResultMessage.structured_output. If no valid output is produced within the retry limit, the result subtype is error_max_structured_output_retries.
questions.key_takeaway: Use output_format for validated JSON results instead of parsing free text.

questions.question: A hospital wants a clinical-notes agent processing PHI under its HIPAA BAA and asks for "a hosted agent with no infrastructure to manage." Which design fits?

options.text: Claude Managed Agents in a US environment, because keeping data in a US region satisfies HIPAA by itself.
options.why_wrong: Managed Agents is not currently eligible for HIPAA BAA coverage; geography doesn't change eligibility.

options.text: Claude Managed Agents with session deletion after each run, which makes the service eligible for a BAA.
options.why_wrong: Deleting sessions is possible, but the service is still stateful by design and not BAA-eligible.

options.text: A self-hosted environment for Managed Agents, since running the sandbox on-premises transfers BAA scope.
options.why_wrong: Sessions and history are still stored server-side by the Managed Agents service; eligibility is unchanged.

options.text: Its own agent loop (e.g. the Agent SDK) on a BAA-eligible configuration, using only eligible features.

questions.explanation: Managed Agents is stateful by design: it stores conversation history, sandbox state and outputs server-side, so it is not currently eligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA BAA coverage. Compliance picks the wiring path before convenience does.
questions.key_takeaway: Rule out Managed Agents for ZDR or HIPAA workloads; run your own loop on an eligible configuration.

questions.question: A Managed Agents session running in an Anthropic cloud environment must call your internal pricing service, which is reachable only from inside your VPC. How do you wire this?

options.text: Add the service URL to the environment's limited networking allowlist so the container can call it.
options.why_wrong: An allowlist cannot make a VPC-only service reachable from Anthropic's cloud container.

options.text: Declare it as a custom tool: the session emits agent.custom_tool_use and your backend replies.
Put the service's API key in the agent's system prompt so the built-in toolset can call it.
options.why_wrong: Secrets don't belong in prompts, and the service still isn't reachable from the sandbox.

options.text: Mount the service's repository as a github_repository resource so the agent can run it.
options.why_wrong: Running a copy of the code in the sandbox is not calling your VPC service.

questions.explanation: Custom tools ({"type": "custom"}) pause the session and emit agent.custom_tool_use. Your backend runs the logic where the service is reachable and posts user.custom_tool_result. Use Vaults (vault_ids) to keep credentials out of the container.
questions.key_takeaway: Use Managed Agents custom tools for logic that must run in your own environment.

questions.question: A TypeScript Agent SDK service passes env: { API_TOKEN: token } in its options, and every run fails at startup with a spawn ENOENT error. What is the cause?

options.text: API_TOKEN collides with a reserved SDK variable name, so the CLI refuses to start at all.
options.why_wrong: No such reserved-name conflict explains ENOENT; the executable can't be found on PATH.

options.text: TypeScript requires allowDangerouslySkipPermissions whenever a custom env object is passed.
options.why_wrong: That flag is required only for bypassPermissions, not for env.

options.text: In TypeScript, env replaces process.env, so PATH is lost; spread process.env into the object.
The SDK cannot use a locally installed CLI, so the binary has to be installed globally first.
options.why_wrong: Installation location isn't the issue; the wiped PATH is.

questions.explanation: Python's options.env merges onto the process environment, but TypeScript's replaces process.env. Without PATH the CLI can't be spawned, so pass { ...process.env, API_TOKEN: token }.
questions.key_takeaway: In TypeScript, always spread process.env into options.env or PATH is lost.
